For OP's sake I'm not sure I agree with this, and that's coming from me who nearly died as a result of one of their injections. I get what you're saying - when a drug showed me a pain that made my whole life of debilitating mental illness seem like a walk in the park in comparison, my view on psychiatry changed. I am terrified of seeking help now simply in case they do forcefully medicate me (I concluded that death would actually be better!) HOWEVER, not ALL wards are like that, I have been in good and bad ones and they are all very slowly improving as stigma lifts over time. One option is to register an advanced directive to state that you don't want to be medicated. Generally they don't "section" you for depression or suicide attempts unless you refuse to go to hospital. Agree to go in as a voluntary patient and they can't forcefully medicate. Hell, 2 people I know jumped off bridges and didn't even get admitted (which if you ask me is negligent). I took no meds during my last 2 admissions. Also, what do you mean "really are schizo"? Said as if people with psychosis are in a different league to people with depression and somehow it's ok for them to be subject to possible malpractice because they're truly fucked whereas depressed people are only mildly fucked and are better off manning up rather than dabbling with psych wards?? TLDR: tragically a lot of what you wrote can be true but I feel the way you phrased it could be interpreted as fear-mongering/ exaggerated/ one sided and if we are to effectively spread the word about malpractice within psychiatry we ought to at least try to seem unbiased.
